subject: ACME RAG eval — retriever/reranker next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: ACME RAG eval — initial post-call recap and next steps

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking time today — really appreciate the thoughtful product context. Quick recap and what we recommend as next steps so we can get a focused RAG eval running in your environment: 

Call recap (high level):
- Primary use: internal knowledge base + policy search for support agents (short answers + grounded excerpts).
- Target latency: 300–500ms for user-facing single-turn queries; batch analytics queries can be higher.
- Accuracy goal: >90% grounding accuracy on critical policy Qs, low hallucination for regulatory content.
- Current infra: Elasticsearch-backed docs (chunked, ~1–3k tokens each after split).

Recommended model & eval plan (short):
1) Retriever: use dense retrieval with embeddings + hybrid sparse signals. We recommend starting with your existing ES vector index + embeddings from text-embed-3-small (or equivalent) for parity. See attachment retriever-config.json for suggested hyperparams (chunk size 800 tokens, overlap 200, top_k=100 for prefilter).
2) Reranker: cross-encoder reranker for production accuracy on high-value queries (redwood-reranker-cross-enc-v2). Pipeline: retrieve top-100 (fast vector) -> rerank top-20 -> final top-5. This balances recall and latency.
3) Generator: for short answer synthesis we suggest a mid-sized tuned generator (redwood-13b-q4f) to start; upgrade to a higher-capacity model only if you need longer form synthesis.

Grounding & metrics to track in the eval:
- Precision@1 and Recall@k (k=5,20)
- MRR (mean reciprocal rank)
- Grounding accuracy (human-labeled test set)
- Hallucination incidence on sensitive policy queries
- End-to-end latency (95th pct)

Attachments & links:
- acme-benchmark-results.csv (sample export)
- retriever-config.json (suggested retrieval hyperparams)
- prompt-sets-acme.csv (seed prompts + expected grounding tags)
- Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cACME-RAG-benchmarks

Next steps / owners:
- Marissa (me): I’ll send the initial eval harness + seed prompt set (attached).
- Neha: can you provision a sandbox deployment with dedicated quota for a 48–72h run?
- Vivek: I’ll loop you in for the regression plan and SLA questions; can you share the internal eval harness?
- Samir: please confirm which subset of policies you want prioritized (Security, Billing, Product) and availability for a 30-min follow-up next week.

We’ll start with a 2-stage eval: (A) offline metrics on your seed prompts + labeled grounding set; (B) small shadow deployment with traffic mirroring for latency/UX checks.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate times via calendar if you give availability.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A couple of clarifying questions before we spin up the sandbox:

1) Retrieval window: our docs vary widely in length — for short policy Qs do you expect chunking at 800 tokens to capture context without creating too many false positives? Any recommendations for chunk overlap vs recall tradeoffs?
2) Reranker latency: cross-encoder sounds right for quality, but what latency hit should we expect for the re-rank stage (per-query)? We’re concerned about staying under the 300–500ms SLO.
3) Regression testing: we have an existing labeled set (~600 examples). Will Redwood’s eval harness support periodic regression checks and a baseline to compare after model updates?

Also can you share the seed prompt csv and the specific benchmark doc you referenced? Would like to share with internal engineering to prepare data access.

If helpful, I’m available Tue/Wed 10–12 PT next week for the follow-up.

Subject: Re: ACME RAG eval — initial post-call recap and next steps

Great questions — answers inline and a proposed plan:

1) Chunking & overlap: 800-token chunks with 200-token overlap is a pragmatic default for policy docs. It keeps most answers in a single chunk while keeping the index size manageable. For extremely short docs we lower to 400 tokens. If you observe precision loss in the offline run we can increase overlap or use semantic chunk joins for specific doc types.

2) Reranker latency: expect an added 30–120ms per query for a well-optimized cross-encoder reranker (depending on model size and GPU profile). Our suggested pipeline (pre-rank top-100 -> rerank top-20 -> final top-5) often keeps end-to-end p95 within 300–500ms on Dedicated capacity; for hosted parity we can A/B with a bi-encoder + lightweight title-match heuristic for lower-latency traffic. We’ll surface concrete latency numbers from the sandbox run.

3) Regression testing support: yes — Redwood Optimize includes a regression harness that will run your labeled set on every model change. We’ll snapshot baseline metrics (precision@1, grounding accuracy, hallucination-rate) and send alerts for major regressions. Vivek, I’ll let you provide access to the harness repo and the small CI config we use.

Seed assets attached: prompt-sets-acme.csv (seed prompts + expected grounding label), and I uploaded the full benchmark sheet to the Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2B3cACME-RAG-benchmarks

Concrete next steps and timeline: 
- Today: Neha will provision a 72h sandbox with dedicated quota (Neha, are you good to start this afternoon?).
- By Thu EOD: Run offline eval on seed set + labeled 600 examples; we’ll share CSV results and key metrics.
- Next Tue/Wed: 30-min follow-up to review results and decide on production rollout cadence.

Owners:
- Marissa: coordinate follow-up and share evaluation report.
- Neha: sandbox provisioning + run orchestration.
- Vivek: regression config + baseline snapshot.

If that works, Samir can we lock Tue 11:00 AM PT? I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
